_readme: Evidence for Krea 2, and the phase's sharpest example of why local and hosted
The HOSTED Krea 2 Large endpoint accepts ten references, each with an independent
0-1 strength and positive or negative guidance. That is a real per-reference weight,
and it is the reason CineBraid's capability vocabulary has a referenceWeights flag
The PUBLISHED WEIGHTS are text-to-image only. Krea's own model card for Krea 2 Turbo
documents no image-to-image, no reference images and no editing. Carrying the hosted
endpoint's ten weighted references onto the open checkpoint would put an approved
identity reference on a local render that has nowhere to receive it.
An earlier draft of this record had openWeights null on the strength of a provider
describing an endpoint as open-source. That was too weak a source for the claim and
also, as it turns out, understated the truth: Krea publishes both checkpoints, an
inference repository and a licence. The correction is recorded rather than quietly
applied, because the reason the first answer was wrong is worth keeping.

openCheckpoints.role: undistilled base, published for fine-tuning, post-training and LoRA training

license.name: Krea 2 Community License
license.note: A commercial licence is offered separately. The terms have NOT been read and must be before anything ships on these weights.

identity.note: Krea 2 Raw is NOT given its own catalogue entry. Its job is to be trained on, not to generate, and giving it a definition would mean inventing a capability difference from Turbo that the vendor does not document. It is recorded here, which is where the LoRA claim on Turbo comes from.

capabilities.value: 12B dense DiT with a Qwen Image VAE and a Qwen3-VL text encoder

capabilities.claim: Krea 2 Turbo is TEXT-TO-IMAGE ONLY in the open release.
capabilities.note: The card documents no image-to-image, reference-image or editing capability.

capabilities.claim: Sampling budget for the distilled checkpoint.
Krea 2 Raw is published as the fine-tuning and LoRA-training base.
capabilities.note: This is what makes local production identity possible for this family without a reference image.

capabilities.claim: Hosted Krea 2 Large accepts weighted reference images.
capabilities.note: Each with an independent 0-1 strength and positive or negative guidance. HOSTED ONLY.

capabilities.claim: Hosted Krea 2 Large exposes a named creativity control rather than a raw CFG number.
Hosted Krea 2 Turbo is text-to-image with no reference images, agreeing with the open checkpoint.

notEstablished.claim: Whether the hosted Krea 2 Large corresponds to Krea 2 Raw, to Krea 2 Turbo, or to neither.
notEstablished.status: no vendor source read connects the hosted variant names to the published checkpoints
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: krea-2/large records openWeights false and inherits NOTHING from the open release. Its ten weighted references stay a hosted capability, and the catalogue caveat says so in the words a filmmaker would read.
constraints.vramGuidanceGb is null. A 12B model is not a light one, and CineBraid does not publish a number it cannot cite.
Recorded as a caveat on the catalogue entry. This is why Z-Image Turbo under Apache 2.0 is the launch local option and Krea 2 Turbo is next-up.

notEstablished.claim: A maximum output resolution for the open checkpoint.
notEstablished.status: the card demonstrates 1024 and 2048 and publishes no ceiling
notEstablished.cineBraidBehaviour: constraints.resolutions is null, meaning unrestricted rather than those two sizes only.

conflicts.resolution: Not a contradiction - three different things. Recorded as three rows against three surfaces. krea-2/turbo carries a surfaceCapabilities block whose local and api faces agree at zero, which turns 'the open checkpoint takes no references' from an assumption into an observation.

cineBraidGap.referenceWeights: CineBraid can REFUSE a weighted reference correctly and cannot yet EXPRESS one: a plan reference carries a role, a source and production meaning, but no strength. Encoding this family made the gap visible, which is the point of encoding a model before wiring it.
